title: Create Diwali Lamps
strapline: Small clay lamps shaped, dried and decorated — the Festival of Lights made with our own hands.
intent: Children are introduced to Diwali, the Festival of Lights, through making rather than being told about it.
Shaping, pinching and pressing builds real hand strength and fine motor control.
Decorating with gems and sequins invites genuine creative choice and pride in the result.
Children learn that light carries meaning in celebrations across many families.
A two-stage make — shape it, let it dry, come back and decorate — teaches patience.
implementation: Provide clay, dough or paper and paint so every child can shape a small lamp of their own.
Model pinching and pressing a hollow, then let children solve the shape themselves.
Leave the lamps to dry properly and return to them the next day to decorate — the wait is part of it.
Offer paint, gems, glitter and sequins and let children choose their own decoration.
Tell the Diwali story of light simply and truthfully while hands are busy.
Invite families who celebrate to share what their own lamps look like at home.
Light the finished lamps with battery tea lights and dim the room to see the effect together.
key_questions: How can you make a hollow in your lamp for the light to sit in?
What will you use to decorate yours?
Why do you think people light lamps at Diwali?
How does the room look different when all our lamps are lit?
Does anyone in your family light lamps or candles at a special time?

impact.text: Children learn that families celebrate differently and find that interesting.
Children make real choices about how to decorate and own the result proudly.
Children shape and manipulate materials with growing hand strength and control.
Children create with a plan and adapt it when the material will not do as they hoped.
Children pick up and use new vocabulary from the celebration and the making.
Children wait through the drying stage and come back to finish what they started.

enhancements: A rangoli pattern table with coloured rice or sand alongside the lamps.
A home corner set for Diwali with tea lights, toy food and flowers.
A family sharing session where children explain their lamp to a visitor.
A light-and-dark investigation — torches, mirrors, coloured cellophane.
A comparison display of lamps, candles and lanterns from several celebrations.
A story session with a picture book about Diwali kept in the book corner all half-term.

playing_exploring: Children explore what clay and dough will do under their hands.
An open decoration table invites genuine, unguided choice.
active_learning: The two-day make demands patience and children come back to finish.
Children concentrate hard on a small, fiddly, satisfying task.
creating_thinking: Children plan a lamp and adjust when the shape collapses or cracks.
They connect their own making to a real celebration with real meaning.
